SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: iter-13 (+300-param FoE prox) gave hr 0.0 -- PSNR 34.3 < baseline. NOT undertrained (loss converged 3.8e-3->4.4e-5 by ep5, gains engaged ~0.28). READ: a learned FoE ISOTROPIC smoother FIGHTS filtered-DC -- fbp(Rx-g) already produces a complete ramp-filtered reconstruction each step, so an added smoothing prior just OVER-SMOOTHS the recon the DC just made (the FoE solves the streak-smearing problem filtered-DC ALREADY solved -> pure drag). So on filtered-DC, isotropic prox capacity is a LIABILITY. (2) FAILURE MODE (iter-13): isotropic prox over-smooths the filtered-DC reconstruction. (3) ONE KNOB: add a DIRECTIONAL (oriented) streak reg on the LEAN bilateral path (I edited build_reg to compose ComposedBilateralAnisotropicReg -- bilateral gate + AnisotropicOrientedReg, NO FoE). +3 params (2 sigma along/across + 1 zero-init gain over 4 fixed orientations) -> 16 total. Zero-init gain => reg==bilateral==champion BYTE-FOR-BYTE at init (worst case == 0.4345, no regression). (4) HYPOTHESIS: unlike the isotropic FoE, the oriented reg smooths ALONG residual streak directions while PRESERVING across them, so it removes the specific directional streaks filtered-DC leaves WITHOUT the isotropic over-smoothing that killed iter-13 -> hr climbs past 0.4345. This is the sparse-view-NATIVE prox form (streaks are directional). (5) BUDGET: K=30 filtered + lean bilat + aniso (analytic oriented kernels, cheap), train_n=200, max_train_s=1080, --time=00:30:00, 200-val -> 20-min comparable.
